mainText: This is Dose of Good for Sunday, November 22. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Helicopter rescues two women trapped in a Brazilian canyon. Stranded since Thursday by a flash flood on the Fumacinha waterfall trail, the women, aged 48 and 64, were lifted out of a 280-metre canyon by an officer who rappelled down. Both were brought out safely. Second: Daily pill halts pancreatic cancer growth in trial. In a trial of 61 patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy stopped tumour growth in almost all of them. At one year, 76.6% were alive, versus 40–45% on standard chemo. Longer studies are needed. Third: Volunteers have saved 3,000 freshwater turtles in Australia. The 1 Million Turtles project has about 40,000 citizen records, protected 2,468 nests and rescued over 3,000 turtles from roads. It could add a million hatchlings in coming decades. Fourth: British island's seabirds rebound from 6,000 to 48,000. After rats were eradicated from Lundy, seabirds came back in force. The UK's first no-take marine zone, created with local fishers, is full of lobsters that now spill into nearby fishing grounds. Fifth: São Paulo universities showcase technology for people with disabilities. At Brazil's Paralympic Training Centre, a showcase featured AI games for neurodivergent pupils, modular wheelchairs, exoskeletons and sign-language translation, backed by about R$10 million. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
